title: Surge Vessel
model_title: Surge Vessel (Air-Cushion Type) for Water-Hammer Protection

introduction.definition: A surge vessel protects pipelines from water hammer. When a pump trips or a valve closes, a pressure wave travels along the pipe; the vessel's compressed-air cushion lets water flow out or in, damping the pressure swings and preventing vacuum.
applications: Pumped water mains and irrigation lines
Cooling water and fire water systems
introduction.summary: A surge vessel protects a pipeline from water hammer. When a pump trips or a valve closes quickly, pressure waves travel along the pipe; the vessel's compressed-air cushion lets water flow in or out, damping the pressure rise and preventing column separation (vacuum).

video_tutorials.title: Surge Vessel — Introduction

script.narration: This module introduces the Surge Vessel.
A surge vessel protects pipelines from water hammer.
When a pump trips or a valve closes, a pressure wave travels along the pipe; the vessel's compressed-air cushion lets water flow out or in, damping the pressure swings and preventing vacuum.
Typical applications include pumped water mains and irrigation lines; sewage rising mains; cooling water and fire water systems; oil pipelines (bladder type).
The cutaway reveals the internal construction.
The exploded view separates every component so each one can be tapped for its function, material and failure modes.
Next, watch the operation tutorial to see how it works.

video_tutorials.title: Surge Vessel — Operation

script.narration: How the Surge Vessel works.
In normal running the air cushion is compressed to line pressure.
When the pump trips, water flows out of the vessel into the main, preventing vacuum.
When the reverse wave returns, water flows back in and compresses the air.
The compressor tops up air that dissolves over time.
The flow overlay traces the liquid from suction to discharge.

video_tutorials.title: Surge Vessel — Maintenance

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Surge Vessel.
Check water level/air volume.
Service compressor; test relief valve.
Internal inspection.
Watch for loss of air cushion: vessel full of water; surges unprotected. Common cause: air dissolved, compressor fault.
Watch for over-pressure: high transient pressures. Common cause: undersized/incorrect pre-charge.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
